$comment: Kichler (landscape and architectural lighting) runs a headless-CMS site (Contentful assets, Next.js-style app) with product pages at /<slug>-<model> (5,979 URLs in sitemap.xml). The product price is only in the page's schema.org Product JSON-LD ($22.99 on the sample): the visible page shows no price element, so the selectors cannot read it. The image is og:image and the description is the meta description; the product name is the h1, whose text carries the size and model. fetch.engine is default (APP_DEFAULT_ENGINE, ai-crawler-avalai on this instance): the LLM reads the JSON-LD price (2299 cents, available) and returns the image and the attribute rows as specs (6 on the sample: attribute, height, length, width, finish), each checked against the page, at about 5,200+900 tokens per request. The selectors are the http fallback and the saved fixture (title, image and description). Engines tried on the sample on 2026-11-19: http: not configured for price; the fallback fields read on http; browser: the same page (the price is not in the rendered markup); ai-crawler-avalai (AI page fetch over http and browser): SUCCESS with price $22.99, image, description and 6 specs; web_search: SEARCH_NO_RESULT. ai-crawler-avalai is selected because it returns the price. Needs APP_AI_CRAWLER_ENABLED with an AvalAI key on the instance. Checked against the saved (curl) 2-fixture mount in Centennial Brass page on 2026-11-19.
